page: Amazon Web Services inf2.48xlarge is a dedicated accelerated computing instance designed for large-scale deep learning inference workloads. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform is driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, delivering 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 768.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Specialized acceleration is provided by 12 integrated AWS Inferentia2 processors delivering a combined 384 GB of accelerator VRAM. The system features a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data needs.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate exceptional compute throughput across parallel workloads. The system achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark multi-threaded evaluations, including strong performance in CPU encryption and extended instruction processing. In high-concurrency memory and caching operations, the server delivers 172.89 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier cached memory bandwidth exceeding 11,700 GB/sec. Large language model inference evaluations highlight strong prompt processing speeds across small and medium model sizes, achieving 2,781.74 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 219.27 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. Single-threaded metrics, including standard decompression and synthetic memory benchmarks, show average to lower relative scores compared to raw parallel execution.

The dense integration of 12 Inferentia2 accelerators alongside 192 high-frequency CPU cores provides favorable resource density for throughput-critical model serving without the operational overhead of general-purpose discrete GPUs. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning dataset caching and persistent artifact retrieval must leverage network interfaces via the 100 Gbps fabric. The instance is suited for large-scale language model inference, generative AI serving, natural language processing pipelines, batch inference tasks, and high-concurrency microservices requiring deep learning acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services inf2.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for deep learning inference. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, the system provides 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, paired with 768 GB of DDR4 system memory. Acceleration is driven by 12 AWS Inferentia2 chips yielding 384 GB of total VRAM. The instance features a 100 Gbps baseline network interface and includes no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, inf2.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU compute, PassMark encryption performance, and 172.89 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside strong prompt processing throughput on small and medium LLM models. The combination of high accelerator density and dedicated host compute makes this instance well matched for production transformer model serving, LLM batch inference, real-time natural language processing, and distributed deep learning deployment.
